rows.rationale: EU ADS type-approval rules are dedicated and UNECE technical harmonisation is advanced, while lawful operation, actors and infrastructure remain partly national and fragmented.
rows.bridge: Art 34bis agency/deeming; Art 39 equivalence/exemption; national operational law remains necessary
rows.sensitivity: Road/actor/liability plausibly N1–N2; technical and international remain N3.
rows.robust_conclusion: Technical/international-leading configuration survives all plausible ±1 recoding.
rows.caveat: This is a supranational baseline, not a self-contained road-operation jurisdiction.

rows.rationale: The 2024 Act creates dedicated responsible actors and authorisation architecture; 2026 APS permits enable passenger-service deployment while the full authorisation framework and final safety principles are still being implemented.
rows.family: Actor / institutional-leading configuration with staged operational permitting
rows.bridge: APS permit bridge before full 2027 AV Act implementation
rows.sensitivity: Operation N2–N3; actor/liability N2–N3; international N1–N2.
rows.robust_conclusion: Actor/institution-leading configuration survives plausible recoding; legal institutionalisation precedes routine general deployment.
rows.caveat: General full-Act implementation is planned for 2027; APS is a targeted early route, not proof that all AV use is N3.

rows.rationale: Croatia combines EU technical approval with dedicated road-traffic rules, remote/intervention actors, owner enforcement duties and a mandatory service-level real-world validation procedure before public passenger transport.
rows.bridge: Mandatory real-world service validation on a registered sample vehicle before passenger service
rows.sensitivity: Liability N2–N3; infrastructure N1–N2; international N2–N3.
rows.robust_conclusion: Deployment-assurance configuration remains robust under conservative recoding.
rows.caveat: Civil liability and quantitative retesting/change-control rules remain less clear than traffic-offence and service-assurance rules.

rows.rationale: EU technical approval can reach N3, but current Slovak law still relies mainly on § 49 conditional test operation for AV/FAV; dedicated general operator/control-centre/fully automated deployment rules are proposed in print 1329 but are not yet law.
rows.bridge: § 49 test-operation permit; narrower ADV operational regime
rows.sensitivity: Road/actor/behaviour plausibly N1–N2 because of permits and the narrower automated-delivery-vehicle regime; technical stays N3.
rows.robust_conclusion: Testing-permit / technical-leading configuration persists under plausible recoding and after the 1 September 2026 trial-focused amendment.
rows.caveat: Snapshot is 25 August 2026. Print 1329 passed first reading but committee deadlines fall in September; Act 131/2026 is adopted but effective only from 1 September 2026.

rows.rationale: France combines EU vehicle approval with a dedicated automated-road-transport-system regime requiring safety demonstration for the technical system and deployed route or zone, qualified independent assessment, remote-intervention qualifications, safety management and a formal service-organiser decision before operation.
rows.family: Deployment-assurance configuration – system safety-case / organiser-decision variant
rows.bridge: Prior safety demonstration + qualified-body opinions + organiser decision of mise en service
rows.sensitivity: Liability N2-N3; infrastructure N1-N2; international N2-N3.
rows.robust_conclusion: Deployment-assurance configuration remains robust, with a safety-case/organiser-decision gate rather than Croatia’s service-test gate.
rows.caveat: Dedicated criminal responsibility is clear; civil-liability allocation is less comprehensively AV-specific and is therefore coded conservatively at N2.

rows.interpretation: The amendment broadens/adjusts § 49 trial mechanics but does not itself create a general deployment/operator regime.
rows.rationale: The amendment broadens/adjusts § 49 trial mechanics but does not itself create a general deployment/operator regime.

rows.regime_label: Slovakia if print 1329 enacted substantially as proposed
rows.interpretation: Would move Slovakia from test-permit accommodation toward dedicated institutionalisation, while infrastructure and cross-border operational recognition would remain less mature.
rows.rationale: Would move Slovakia from test-permit accommodation toward dedicated institutionalisation, while infrastructure and cross-border operational recognition would remain less mature.

pathways.pattern: Technical and/or international layers are at least one stage ahead of operational/actor layers.
pathways.value: Shows why type approval cannot be treated as equivalent to lawful deployment.

pathways.pattern: Dedicated responsible actors and liability/authorisation architecture precede full ordinary operational implementation.
pathways.value: Falsifies one-directional pacing accounts: law can lead deployment.

pathways.pattern: Vehicle technical approval is followed by a separate service or system-level safety gate before ordinary operation.
pathways.case: Croatia - real-world service-test gate; France - safety-case + qualified assessment + organiser mise-en-service decision
pathways.value: Portability result: the pathway repeats across jurisdictions even though the bridging mechanism differs.

pathways.pattern: Public-road access remains predominantly experimental/conditional despite advanced technical standards.
pathways.value: Illustrates persistent inter-layer mismatch and dependence on legal bridges.

findings.Cross-sectional finding: The five 2026 regimes do not line up on one common ladder. They display different layer configurations and different leading layers. France strengthens the model because it replicates the deployment-assurance family through a different legal mechanism than Croatia.
findings.Novelty implication: The strongest defensible contribution is a vector/pathway model: jurisdiction-specific configurations of functional-layer states produce recurring pathway families, while legal bridges or gates differ in doctrinal form.
findings.Next empirical step: A true inter-coder reliability test requires a second human coder. The present same-model rule-based second pass is sufficient as a sensitivity audit, so theoretical drafting can now proceed.

audit.rule: Require dedicated AV-specific liability institutionalisation for N2+
Require dedicated reciprocal operational recognition, not only participation in UNECE technical instruments
Dedicated traffic-offence and owner responsibility is insufficient for N3 without mature AV-specific civil-liability allocation
Draft operator and control-centre roles are excluded; narrower ADV and trial roles do not establish general FAV institutionalisation
Dedicated criminal responsibility exists, but N3 requires a broader stable AV-specific liability and risk architecture
Route and zone infrastructure is integrated into the safety case, but infrastructure is not yet routinised as an ordinary AV-wide layer

purpose: Cross-sectional Validation – Regulatory Normalisation of Automated Vehicles (snapshot: 25 August 2026)

Purpose: test whether the N0–N4 functional-layer model discriminates among contemporary regimes at the same point in time. Scores measure legal embedding, not regulatory intensity. Draft law is excluded from current-law scores and shown separately as sensitivity/prospective evidence.
